summary_paragraph: A homeless woman with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and recurrent urinary issues was admitted for foul-smelling urine, right flank pain, and worsening frostbite of the right foot. She received a femoral central line for access and was started on Levaquin in the ED. Labs showed no fever or leukocytosis, and urine cultures revealed mixed flora, suggesting contamination rather than active infection. Blood cultures grew Corynebacterium species from both sets, but due to lack of clinical signs, it was presumed to be a contaminant and not treated. Frostbite was managed with wound care and ibuprofen, with possible tissue loss in the right hallux. The patient declined further hospitalization and left against medical advice with the femoral line still in place. She was advised on wound care, follow-up with urology for a suprapubic catheter, and safe line removal, but discharged to home despite recommendations for supervised care.
problems: Accident due to excessive cold due to weather conditions
Late effect of spinal cord injury
Late effects of injury, undetermined whether accidentally or purposely inflicted
